drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: For discussion and subject to our client's approval, we propose a purchase price of USD 8,000,000 as part of the complete package below. We have proposed simultaneous payment and transfer, specified Closing mechanics and termination rights, and a defined financial-statement and indemnity framework. Seller and Shares particulars remain bracketed pending verification; we cannot responsibly supply unconfirmed facts. Please provide your client's position on the package and identify any required regulatory approvals. No provision is agreed in isolation, and all proposals remain subject to execution of a definitive agreement.

edits.text: PARTIES AND SHARES. This Agreement is between [Seller's full legal name, jurisdiction and entity type/address] as Seller and Meridian Acquisitions LLC as Buyer. The “Shares” means [number] [class] shares in [issuer's full legal name and jurisdiction], constituting [percentage]% of its issued share capital. These particulars must be verified and completed before execution.

1. PURCHASE PRICE. The proposed purchase price for the Shares is USD 8,000,000, subject to Seller's approval and agreement on the complete transaction terms. At Closing, Buyer shall pay the agreed purchase price without deduction or setoff by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by Seller in writing and independently verified by Buyer. Payment and transfer of the Shares shall occur simultaneously under Clause 2.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur by electronic exchange on a mutually agreed date no later than thirty calendar days after execution (the “Long-Stop Date”). Closing is conditional upon receipt of the mandatory approvals and third-party consents expressly identified in an agreed schedule, absence of any legal prohibition on the transaction, and each party's material performance of its pre-Closing obligations. Neither party has a financing condition. Seller shall deliver duly executed transfer instruments, share certificates or agreed evidence of uncertificated ownership, evidence of its authority, and the issuer's acknowledgment of registration of Buyer as holder effective upon payment. Buyer shall deliver the purchase price and evidence of its authority. Documents may be held to order pending confirmation of receipt of funds; no transfer or release shall take effect unless payment and all required deliveries occur simultaneously. Any additional deliverables or conditions must be expressly agreed in writing before execution. Each party shall use reasonable efforts to satisfy the conditions applicable to it. A condition may be waived only in writing by its beneficiary and only where legally permissible. If Closing has not occurred by the Long-Stop Date, either party may terminate by written notice, unless its own material breach caused the failure to close. Termination ends future performance obligations without affecting accrued claims for breach or provisions expressly stated to survive. The parties may extend the Long-Stop Date by written agreement.

3. REPRESENTATIONS AND DISCLOSURE. “Financial Statements” means the issuer's [audited/unaudited] financial statements for [identified periods], attached as Schedule 1. Seller represents at signing and Closing that the Financial Statements were prepared in accordance with [specified accounting standards], consistently applied, and fairly present in all material respects the issuer's financial position and results for those periods, subject to the qualifications expressly identified in Schedule 1. Seller also represents that it owns the Shares, has authority to transfer them, and will transfer them free of liens. Qualifications and exceptions must be fairly disclosed in a disclosure schedule delivered and agreed before signing, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the relevant matter. General references to a data room do not constitute disclosure. Post-signing disclosures do not qualify these representations or waive a claim without Buyer's express written agreement. The accounting standards, statements, disclosure schedule and any unaudited-statement qualifications must be completed before execution.

4. INDEMNITY. Seller shall indemnify Buyer for actual, documented losses resulting from a breach of Clause 3 or an Undisclosed Liability, without double recovery. “Undisclosed Liability” means a liability of the issuer arising from acts, omissions or circumstances occurring before Closing that was neither recorded or specifically reserved for in the Financial Statements nor fairly disclosed in the agreed disclosure schedule, excluding ordinary-course liabilities incurred after the latest Financial Statements date that do not arise from breach of contract or law. Claims other than claims concerning title, authority or Seller's own fraud must be notified within twelve months after Closing; Seller is liable only for aggregate qualifying losses exceeding one percent of the purchase price, and only for the excess, with aggregate liability capped at ten percent of the purchase price. Title and authority claims must be notified within three years after Closing, are not subject to the deductible, and, together with all other non-fraud claims, are capped at the purchase price. These limits do not restrict liability for Seller's own fraud or liability that applicable law prohibits limiting. A timely notified claim survives until resolved. Notices must describe the factual basis and a good-faith estimate of loss, if reasonably ascertainable. Buyer shall give prompt notice of third-party claims; delay reduces recovery only to the extent Seller is materially prejudiced, subject to the applicable claim deadline. Seller may assume the defense with reasonably acceptable counsel after acknowledging its indemnification obligation, but not where there is a material conflict of interest or material nonmonetary relief is sought against Buyer or the issuer. Buyer may participate at its own expense. No settlement may impose an admission, nonmonetary obligation or unreimbursed payment on Buyer or the issuer without Buyer's written consent, not unreasonably withheld. Buyer shall reasonably mitigate losses; recoveries shall be reduced by insurance and third-party proceeds actually received, net of reasonable recovery costs. Punitive damages are excluded except to the extent payable to a third party. Following Closing, this Clause is the exclusive monetary remedy for matters within its scope, except for Seller's own fraud; it does not limit enforcement of payment obligations or available equitable relief.

Open factual items: confirm Seller's identity and authority, issuer, share class and number, ownership percentage, transfer restrictions and registration mechanics. Do not execute with these particulars incomplete.

All price and risk-allocation terms are proposed as a package and subject to client approval. Before execution, complete the schedules and agree governing law, dispute resolution, notices, confidentiality, costs and tax allocation, and other necessary definitive-agreement provisions.

receiver.message_back: Subject to our client’s approval and definitive documentation, Buyer counters at USD 7,500,000 with simultaneous payment and transfer, an 18-month general claims period, a 0.5% tipping basket, a 20% general indemnity cap, and 10% of the price held in escrow for 18 months as security rather than a recovery limit, retaining the proposed title, authority and fraud protections. All particulars, schedules and remaining definitive terms must be agreed before execution; required regulatory approvals cannot be identified responsibly until the issuer’s business, jurisdictions and ownership details are verified, and the closing timetable must accommodate any mandatory clearance.
